text: Some days of bitter grief having passed, a change came over my friend, and his pale face grew, if possible, even paler. <break time="0.8s" /> He wandered from room to room without purpose, and sometimes he sat for hours staring into empty space, as if listening to some imaginary sound. <break time="0.8s" /> On the seventh or eighth night after we had placed her in the vault, I could not sleep, and an unknown fear crept into my heart. <break time="0.8s" /> Soon Usher knocked gently at my door and entered with a lamp, and in his eyes there was a kind of wild, held back excitement. <break time="0.8s" /> And you have not seen it, he said, and he threw open a window to the storm, which was wild yet strangely beautiful. <break time="0.8s" /> The heavy clouds were flying in all directions, and a strange, glowing mist hung around the house, though there was neither moon nor lightning. <break time="0.8s" /> Closing the window, I began to read aloud an old romance called Mad Trist by Sir Launcelot Canning, hoping that it would calm my friend. <break time="0.8s" /> When I read how the hero Ethelred broke down a wooden door, there came from a distant part of the house a cracking and ripping sound. <break time="0.8s" /> Then the story told of a dragons terrible shriek, and at that very moment I heard a long, harsh, screaming sound from somewhere far away.
